samples.summary: getSelectedBlocks() hand-rolls a third copy of the "which blocks does this DocRange cover" traversal instead of driving the module the repo designated as the single one (model/range-slices.ts)
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` opens with: "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers... Rather than keep two copies of the dispatch in sync, both sides drive this module", and `visitRangeSlices` already implements exactly the case this diff adds — "Cross-block inside one cell — the cell's own block list is the document order to walk" (lines 165-190), resolving through `doc.blockParentMap`, plus the same-block-in-a-cell case (151-158). The new code (text-editor.ts:3780-3789) re-derives the same answer from `layout.blockParentMap` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` + index slicing in `sliceBlockRange`. The two now disagree by construction: the new copy path resolves cells inside *nested* tables, while `visitRangeSlices` deliberately does not ("The table case is not recursive", range-slices.ts:140-143). Same question, two answers, free to drift further — the exact failure mode range-slices.ts was written to prevent (issue #715 is cited there). The design doc added in this diff (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md, "Two things make this correct") justifies the choice against `isInTable()`/`getSelectedText()` and never mentions the model-level traversal.

samples.summary: The "every entry point that mutates while an image selection is live clears it" invariant asserted in code and design doc is not exhaustive — table structure ops and insertLink are omitted
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1262-1276 states "Every entry point that mutates text while an image selection can still be live routes through here first" and docs-image-editing.md:284-295 repeats the enumeration (cut, paste, applySpellSuggestion, insertTable, insertImage, insertPageNumber). Grepping `clearImageSelectionForMutation` in editor.ts shows call sites only at 3407, 3498, 3716, 3797 (+ the API alias at 3741). `deleteTable` (3544), `insertTableRow` (3578), `deleteTableRow` (3587), `mergeTableCells` (3628) and `insertLink` (3161) are all toolbar/menu-driven (no preceding keydown to clear the selection) and can delete or restructure the block an image selection names. Cost, per the diff's own reasoning, is a stale `(blockId, offset)` that names a different inline — the next Delete then removes the wrong image. The stated invariant is therefore both untrue and load-bearing.

samples.summary: Read-only suppresses the drawn resize handles but not the resize-cursor hover affordance, so a viewer still gets nwse/ns/ew cursors over invisible handle hotspots
samples.evidence: The change's stated intent (editor.ts:2534-2537, docs-image-editing.md:273-282) is that in read-only "the selection reads as a selection rather than an offer to resize something the viewer cannot resize". But `handleImageHover` (editor.ts:2737-2750) has no `readOnly` guard — it still runs `hitTestImageHandle` on the committed selection rect and sets `cursorForHandle(handle)`. A read-only viewer with an image selected sees resize cursors appear over eight invisible regions and nothing happens on drag: the same false offer the handle removal was meant to withdraw, only harder to explain.

samples.summary: Code comment contradicts the design doc it ships with about whether the context menu offers image copy
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2532-2537 justifies removing the read-only gate as giving the viewer "the image copy the shortcut and the context menu now offer (issue #870)", and editor.ts:1249-1251 says the read-only case is "exactly where the context menu now offers Copy". docs/design/docs/docs-context-menu.md:80-86 states the opposite and is correct: the gate is `getActiveSelection()` (a *text* selection), "the menu never offers Copy for an image in either mode", wiring image selection in being "a straightforward follow-up". `docs-context-menu.tsx:74,181` confirms `showCopy = hasSelection` from `getActiveSelection()`. Future readers get two conflicting statements of the shipped behaviour.

samples.summary: Read-only right-click with only an image selected opens no menu and the native menu is already suppressed, so the image-copy affordance the diff builds has no pointer-driven path
samples.evidence: `hasSelection` comes from `editor.getActiveSelection()` (line 74), which is null when an image is click-selected (`selectImageInline` calls `selection.setRange(null)`). In read-only, `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection` is then false, every group is empty, and the handler returns at line 84 — after `e.preventDefault()` at line 69 already killed the browser menu. The viewer who has just selected an image gets nothing at all from a right-click. The design doc calls this a deliberate follow-up, so it is recorded rather than accidental, but it leaves the new read-only image-copy reachable by keyboard only.
searchedFor: read docs-context-menu.tsx handleContextMenu and group gating

samples.summary: Three distinct concerns bundled into one change: image copy/cut (#870), table-cell copy fidelity (#872), and read-only context-menu Copy
samples.evidence: The diff touches `getSelectedBlocks`/`sliceBlockRange` (#872 — unrelated to images), the image clipboard hooks and read-only image selection (#870), and the frontend context-menu read-only Copy gate (`docs-context-menu.tsx`), plus an unrelated documentation correction to the arrow-key rows of docs-image-editing.md:207-214 ("1px nudge" → "deselect"). Each has its own design doc section and its own failure mode; bundling makes the #872 clipboard-resolution rewrite land behind an image-selection review and makes a partial revert impractical.

samples.summary: drawImageSelection's colour options are dead configurability, widened rather than removed
samples.evidence: `borderColor`/`handleFill`/`handleStroke` are now optional with defaults, but the only production caller is doc-canvas.ts:683, which passes `{ handles: !this.readOnly }` and never a colour. The change converts a required-options object into a partial one solely to add one boolean, keeping three parameters nothing supplies. Dropping them (or passing a mode) would leave a smaller surface.

samples.summary: writeImageToClipboard hand-builds a Block literal instead of the already-imported createBlock() factory
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:1289-1294 spells out `{ id: generateBlockId(), type: 'paragraph', inlines: [...], style: { ...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE } }`, which is `createBlock('paragraph')` (types.ts:374-383) with the inlines replaced. `createBlock` is already imported at text-editor.ts:2. Rather than keep two copies of the dispatch in sync, both sides drive this module", and `visitRangeSlices` already implements exactly the case this diff adds — "Cross-block inside one cell — the cell's own block list is the document order to walk" (lines 165-190), resolving through `doc.blockParentMap`, plus the same-block-in-a-cell case (151-158). The new code (text-editor.ts:3780-3789) re-derives the same answer from `layout.blockParentMap` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` + index slicing in `sliceBlockRange`. The two now disagree by construction: the new copy path resolves cells inside *nested* tables, while `visitRangeSlices` deliberately does not ("The table case is not recursive", range-slices.ts:140-143). verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted, but it is not a blocking design-fit defect. (a) `range-slices.ts:1-17` designates itself as the single traversal for the *inline-style read/write pair* (`Doc.applyInlineStyle` + `visitStyledRunsInRange`, issue #715), a scoping repeated at docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:38-42 — not as the traversal every DocRange consumer must drive. (b) Reuse is not drop-in: `RangeSliceVisitor` yields `(blockId, from, to)` and range-slices.ts:16 states "Empty slices are never reported", while the copy path must emit cloned Blocks preserving type/style/marker/tableData (text-editor.ts:3813-3841) including empty blocks; driving it from visitRangeSlices would drop an empty paragraph mid-selection and violate the issue's acceptance criterion "A cell copy spanning several blocks in one cell keeps each block's type" (todo.md:56). (c) The view layer already owns this layout-based walk: selection.ts:754-785 (`getSelectedText`, pre-existing, untouched) performs the identical blockParentMap→cell→index-slice traversal, and the diff deliberately matches it so clipboard and selection agree. (d) The implemented shape is exactly what the originating task's plan prescribes (todo.md:35-41), and the range-slices re-base is recorded as considered and declined with rationale (todo.md:168-173, 227-229). The residual drift risk is between two different operations (clipboard extraction vs style read/write), so it cannot present a user with two answers to one question; no acceptance criterion is unmet and no stated Non-Goal is crossed. Under this rubric that is minor (reuse available but not required / layer choice with no behavioral consequence), which does not block.

mergedFrom.summary: Code comment contradicts the design doc it ships with about whether the context menu offers image copy
mergedFrom.evidence: editor.ts:2532-2537 justifies removing the read-only gate as giving the viewer "the image copy the shortcut and the context menu now offer (issue #870)", and editor.ts:1249-1251 says the read-only case is "exactly where the context menu now offers Copy". docs/design/docs/docs-context-menu.md:80-86 states the opposite and is correct: the gate is `getActiveSelection()` (a *text* selection), "the menu never offers Copy for an image in either mode", wiring image selection in being "a straightforward follow-up". `docs-context-menu.tsx:74,181` confirms `showCopy = hasSelection` from `getActiveSelection()`. Future readers get two conflicting statements of the shipped behaviour.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the absence itself: deleteTable (editor.ts:3544-3571), insertTableRow (3578-3586), deleteTableRow (3587-3602), mergeTableCells (3628-3640) and insertLink (3161-3230) genuinely do not call clearImageSelectionForMutation, and no wrapper or frontend caller supplies it (the only bulk API loop is the read-only neutralizer at 3903-3921; the only external clearImageSelection() caller is a test, copy-integrity.test.ts:489). But the finding is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (1) The asserted cost is already guarded: deleteSelectedImageInline re-validates the stored (blockId, offset) with findBlock + findImageAtOffset and clears instead of deleting (editor.ts:2282-2303), imageSelectionProvider does the same (2307-2318), and render() resolves the selection by map key so a stale key paints nothing (1893-1895) — so a stale coordinate cannot 'eat the wrong character', and the named table ops restructure blocks without shifting inline offsets in any surviving block. (2) Against the originating work item's acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:51-62) nothing requires exhaustive clearing across all mutation entry points; the clearer was review-driven hardening (ibid. 262-267), so no acceptance criterion is left unmet and no Non-Goal is crossed. What remains is (a) a missing defensive call — a line-level correctness matter explicitly outside this lens (and already carried on the gate as a confirmed correctness finding about the same mechanism) and (b) an over-broad enumeration in the code comment (1261-1273) and design doc (docs-image-editing.md:284-295), which under this rubric is a documented-shape divergence that still behaves as specified: minor, and minor never blocks.
